info.title: OpenAsy Logs API
info.summary: Search what happened on every host and service.
info.description:
Every screen of Logs uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Logs are stored in VictoriaLogs inside the product and searched with [LogsQL](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/logsql/) as it is (ADR 0035). They are sent with a source's ingest token, by syslog, or read over SSH by logs-agent. Each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`). Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description: One JSON object per line, as Vector's http sink (ndjson) and Fluent Bit's http output (json_lines) send. The message, time and level are read from their usual names (message, msg, log; @timestamp, time, ts; level, severity); the rest become fields. Gzip is welcome.
OTLP/HTTP, protobuf or JSON: set the OpenTelemetry Collector's otlphttp exporter logs_endpoint here, with the token as a Bearer header. service.name and host.name become service and host.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` on plain http://localhost).

apiToken.description: An API token from Settings → API tokens (`oa_logs_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

ingestToken.description: A source's ingest token (`olg_...`). `Authorization: ApiKey <token>` works too.

ingestBasic.description: For Elasticsearch outputs: any user name, the ingest token as password.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

oneOf.description: JSON in the message becomes fields; its message, time and level take their places.
Named groups become fields. A group named msg replaces the message, one named time the time.
Names the level alike (error, warn, info...) from words, syslog severities or numbers. field defaults to level.
Replaces what matches, in the message and every field. replacement defaults to ***.
Masks values that look like passwords, tokens, keys and credentials in URLs.
Drops lines whose field matches. field msg is the message.
Keeps percent of the lines whose field matches, and every other line.
Sets a field, such as service for a source that does not send it.

kind.description: http: shippers send with the source's token. syslog: senders in its networks. ssh: hosts logs-agent reads.

networks.description: For syslog: the senders it takes, as addresses or networks.

plain.description: For syslog: also take plain TCP and UDP from these networks, not only TLS.

linesDropped.description: Dropped or sampled away by the pipeline.

processors.description: Defaults to parse-json, map-level and mask-secrets.

token.description: For http sources: the ingest token, shown once (olg_...).

truncated.description: More lines matched than the limit; narrow the query or the range.

shared.description: Seen by everyone; private views only by their owner.

anyOf.description: Checked every minute: when more lines than threshold matched in the window, the webhook is called, and again when it is back under.

webhookSecret.description: Shown once when a threshold is added: verify the webhook-signature header with it (Standard Webhooks).

maxDiskGb.description: 0: the oldest days go when the volume is 90% full.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the certificate senders should pin.

origin.description: file: from the hosts file (OPENASY_HOSTS, ADR 0052); changed there, so PATCH and DELETE answer 409. Fetching its key still works.

fileHostKey.description: The fingerprint hostKey gives in the hosts file: a host that presents that key is trusted without an admin, and no other key can be accepted here.

containers.description: Also read container logs through the host's Docker. Access to the socket is equivalent to root (ADR 0031).

status.description: Of the last read. new and host-key-pending wait for an admin to accept the host key.

unreadable.description: What the account may not read, such as the system journal without the systemd-journal group.

AgentReport.description: What logs-agent says about itself on every call: its version (it must equal logs', ADR 0019), its public keys and the host setup.

Result.description: One of: entries (a read, with where it stopped), hostKeys (the keys a host presents), or error.

more.description: The read stopped at its limit; the host is read again at once.

hostsFile.description: null when OPENASY_HOSTS is not set.

appliedAt.description: When it was last read and applied; null if it never was.

error.description: Why the file on disk is not applied.

warnings.description: What to fix that did not stop the file from being applied, such as a host whose agent is not enrolled yet.

HostsFile.description: The hosts file (ADR 0052), shared with Infrastructure. It is read again within a minute of a change; a file that cannot be applied leaves the hosts from its last good version.
